problem: Evaluate the line integral of the function $f(x,y)=y+1$ along the circle $C$ with equation ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=25.$

activity_context.topic_title: Line Integrals of Scalar Functions Over Circles

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14057418/assets/e27774d260c053a7835b30e62c2d4b41be4b8dc22efcba8f7aa95704590561cf.png)

Evaluate the line integral of the function $f(x,y)=x{e}^{y-3}$ along the circle $C$ with equation ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=16,$ traversed from the point $(0,-4)$ to the point $(4,0),$ as shown above.
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

The curve $C$ is a part-circle of radius $4$ centered at $O.$ It can be parametrized as  

$$
r(t)=⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,4\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,\frac{3\pi }{2}\le t\le 2\pi .
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16{sin}^{2}⁡t+16{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{16({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=x{e}^{y-3},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,{e}^{4\operatorname{sin}⁡t-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,{e}^{4\operatorname{sin}⁡t-3}\cdot 4\cdot \text{d}t \\  & =4{\int }_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,{e}^{4\operatorname{sin}⁡t-3}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this using the substitution $u=4\operatorname{sin}⁡t-3,$ $\text{d}u=4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{\int }_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,{e}^{4\operatorname{sin}⁡t-3}\,\text{d}t & =4{\int }_{-7}^{-3}{e}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =4\,{e}^{u}{|}_{-7}^{-3} \\  & =4({e}^{-3}-{e}^{-7}) \\  & =\frac{4}{{e}^{3}}-\frac{4}{{e}^{7}} \\  & =\frac{4{e}^{4}-4}{{e}^{7}}\end{aligned}
$$
